commentary:
Energy is the morning's story: crude is getting hit hard, with WTI down 3.7% to $89.40 and Brent off 2.4% to just under $100, after reports the EU is weighing the release of 50mn barrels of diesel stockpiles under pressure from Washington — President Trump has threatened to ban US fuel exports if Europe doesn't unlock reserves. Distillates are bearing the brunt: gasoil is down 4.4%, heating oil 3%, and diesel cracks are slumping, while WTI's prompt spread has fallen sharply as backwardation eases.

The selloff is overpowering supportive headlines — Ukraine struck one of Russia's biggest refineries and a key pipeline hub, and the US is adding a carrier and 10,000 troops to the Mideast — so watch whether supply risk reasserts itself once the stockpile headline is digested. The macro backdrop remains one of sticky inflation colliding with fiscal stress. Euro-area September CPI printed 3.8% y/y, Kashkari says US inflation is "still too high," and this week's global bond rout pushed 10-year Treasury yields to their highest since 2002 before steadying.

France is the pressure point: the OAT risk premium hit 150bps over bunds for the first time since 2012, driving a flight-to-quality bid into Buxl (+2.1%) and gilts (+1.1%), hammering euro-zone bank shares and reviving the Swiss franc and yen as havens — note CHF +0.4% this morning. Equity-index futures are nonetheless firmer ahead of September payrolls — S&P +0.5%, Nasdaq +0.7%, DAX +1% — helped by cheaper oil and AI-driven fund inflows.
